synopsis: UN R131 governs heavy-road-vehicle AEBS, including categories M2, M3, N2 and N3; it is an on-road reference, not a regulation applicable to off-road machines merely because they have automatic braking [f2516, f2814, f2514]. Its 02 series entered into force on 4 January 2023 and is identified with EU OJ L 2025/1329 [f2517, f2815]. Requirements include warning at least 0.8 seconds before emergency braking, a braking demand of at least 4 m/s², and category- and test-speed-specific impact limits—for example, 0 km/h impact against a stationary target for heavy hydraulic-brake trucks at test speeds up to 70 km/h [f2519, f2520, f2521]. Testing includes an ISO 19206-2 child pedestrian target crossing at 5 km/h, passing between stationary cars 4.5 metres apart at 50 km/h without warning or braking, and no more than 10% failed runs per robustness category; a failure warning is required within 10 seconds [f2522, f2523, f2525, f2524]. Chapter 8 and the glossary also state that conscious driver action can interrupt automatic braking, with Chapter 8 explicitly extending interruption to warnings; these provisions remain road-vehicle references rather than off-road acceptance requirements [f6323, f13962, f2814].
